newsitem.title: UK: Group in accord to measure Website visits.
newsitem.headline: Group in accord to measure Website visits.

text.p: An international audit group on Wednesday said it agreed to set standards for measuring traffic at World Wide Web sites on the Internet.
The agreement followed the International Federal of Audit Bureaux of Circulations's (IFABC) biennial general assembly in Washington, D.C., last month.

Establishment of a common set of measurement and reporting standards is expected to allow the Web to realize its potential as an advertising medium, the IFABC said. The World Wide Web is the most widely used part of the Internet's international network of computer databases.

"We look forward to helping the interactive industry establish a worldwide currency, which will unlock all the hidden wealth in those Web sites," committee co-chairmen Richard Foan and Lars Bjorkman said in a statement. Foan is deputy chief executive of the UK Audit Bureau of Ciruclation, and Bjorkman is managing director of the Audit Bureau of Circulation in Sweden.

"The September 22 to 27 General Assembly in Washington was an excellent starting point, from which we look forward to a global standard recognised around the world's media buyers," Foan and Bjorkman said.

The IFABC agreed to develop a set of minimum measurement and reporting standards for use by its members and to develop an international trademark that will be included on Web site reports where the standards are used.
